memory_update.text: SOLS is a newly public, underappreciated uranium conversion mapping: formerly hidden inside Honeywell, now a Nasdaq-listed specialty-materials company with the only US UF6 conversion facility at Metropolis Works.
ASPI belongs in the speculative shadow lane for HALEU/enrichment because its exposure depends on technology validation, regulatory approvals, QLE economics, and binding offtake.
LTBR is not a near-term conversion/enrichment bottleneck supplier but may be useful to track as an advanced fuel-design option if reactor customers and regulators validate its technology.

BWXT should be handled in a later pass or as a reference name for advanced fuel fabrication/TRISO; it is relevant but larger, better-covered, and less aligned with this pass's underfollowed small/mid-cap focus.

The investable bottleneck map for nuclear fuel cycle appears uneven: enrichment has LEU and speculative ASPI, conversion now has SOLS, advanced fuel fabrication has fewer clean public names, and private entities such as X-energy/General Matter remain important non-public chokepoints.

node: Nuclear fuel cycle: uranium, conversion, enrichment, HALEU, fabrication
summary: Expanded the nuclear fuel-cycle node with a two-lane universe. The cleanest public chokepoint exposures are not broad nuclear utilities but fuel-cycle specialists or newly separated materials assets. Reference lane: Centrus as the most visible US-listed HALEU/enrichment name. Underfollowed lane: Solstice as the newly public US UF6 conversion asset formerly buried inside Honeywell, plus ASP Isotopes as a sub-$1B speculative enrichment platform. Lightbridge is included as a speculative shadow candidate because it targets advanced nuclear fuel design rather than current conversion/enrichment capacity. No buy/sell view is expressed.
